slides.title: Measuring the Motor's Speed
slides.subtitle: ENGS 28 · Day 12 — In-Class

slides.title: Where we are
items: On Wednesday we read TTmotor_ramp.c one register at a time, and by the end of it we could set the motor to any speed we liked.
In the reading you worked out how to turn a count of pulses from the speed sensor into revolutions per minute.
Today we'll wire that sensor, look at what it says on the oscilloscope, and then build the rest of the Lab 6 system with the measurement in it.
slides.presenterNote: ≈ 2 min, out of a 6-minute bucket that also covers the two transitions into and out of the build. 110 minutes today: 6 settling and transitions, Parts of 8 / 26 / 15 / 13 / 5, 32 for the build with a floor of 25, and 5 for the close. Ask everyone to get the motor setup out now.

slides.title: Wire the sensor and look at what it says
slides.presenterNote: ≈ 26 min, and this is the Part that can eat the hour — it is the only one gated on hardware working for everybody at once. Before anything else: take the scope and the multimeter off Wednesday's PWM node and go back to the bare circuit. Order matters — predict FIRST, then wire, then the states figure. The pull-up never gets cut for time. Her slide 5's standard, and it is the one to hold to: nobody leaves today without pulses on their screen. Groups that get a trace early can start counting the slots on their wheel, which is Part 3's first task.

Where you are, and what is left
items: You have the speed sensor wired, its pulses on the oscilloscope, and the arithmetic that turns them into revolutions per minute.
For Lab 6: the tb6612 driver, the potentiometer mapped to a mode and a speed, the pulse counter on PA15, and the rpm on the display.
The optional experiment at the end of the lab is the 50 Hz one: run the PWM at 50 Hz instead of 1.6 kHz and listen to the motor. The prescaler and reload numbers are Wednesday's.
slides.presenterNote: ≈ 5 min, protected — stop the build for it whatever state the room is in. One minute individual and written first: the stage number you reached, and the first thing you will do tonight. Then round the TABLES, not the individuals — about six tables at fifteen seconds. Then the two items above. The private note before the public round is the difference between a checkpoint and a roll call for a student who is behind. Ask the tables who never got a trace to say so: her standard for today is that nobody leaves without pulses on their screen.
